docs.title: API Docs
docs.subtitle: OpenAI/OpenRouter-compatible API for calling this gateway from outside the panel.
docs.authHelp: All requests use standard OpenAI-style bearer auth. Create a key on the {c1} page — it's shown once, so copy it right away.
docs.auth401: Any request without a valid, active key returns {c1}.
docs.chatHelp: Same request/response shape as OpenAI's Chat Completions API. Routing is always automatic — {c1} must be {c2} or omitted (any other value is rejected with {c3}). The gateway checks each provider's live rate-limit/cooldown state at request time, rotates round-robin across the eligible ones, and fails over automatically if the one it picked hits a limit mid-request. The response's {c4} field always tells you which one actually served the request.
docs.streamingHelp: Returns Server-Sent Events, same chunk format as OpenAI ({c1}, terminated by {c2}).
docs.serverToolsHelp: Add {c1} and the gateway answers questions about this server itself, calling the panel's read-only tools (overview, service status, logs, files) until it can answer. Only read-only access is offered, the key must have been created by an admin, and it can't be combined with your own {c2}.
docs.serverToolsSteps: Every step is reported when it starts and when it finishes. When streaming, it comes as a chunk with an empty {c1} and a {c2} field ({c3}, then {c4}); without streaming, the finished steps are in {c5}.
docs.toolsHelp: Same shape as OpenAI's tool calling: pass {c1} (and optionally {c2} — {c3}, {c4}, {c5}, or a specific {c6}) and the model can respond with {c7} instead of text. Whichever provider actually served the request (Anthropic, Gemini, or an OpenAI-family one) gets this translated to its own native tool format automatically — the request/response shape you see is always OpenAI's.
docs.toolsLoop: To continue the loop, run the function yourself and send its result back as a {c1} role message (with the matching {c2}), alongside the assistant's {c3} message that triggered it:
docs.toolsStream: In streaming mode, {c1} arrive complete in a single chunk (not streamed argument-by-argument) followed by a chunk with {c2}.
docs.visionHelp: Send OpenAI-style content parts: {c1} and {c2}. Images must be inline {c3} URLs (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 10 MB, 8 per message); the gateway does not download image links. Requests with images prefer models tagged {c4}, which get the image itself. A model without {c5} gets the text OCR reads from the image instead.
docs.imagesHelp: OpenAI-compatible image generation, routed automatically to a model tagged {c1} (e.g. {c2}, {c3}) with failover between them. Options: {c4} (required), {c5} (1–4), {c6} (e.g. {c7}; ignored by models that pick their own). Images come back as base64 in {c8}.
docs.transcribeHelp: OpenAI-compatible speech to text (voice notes, calls, recordings), routed automatically to a model tagged {c1} (e.g. {c2} on Groq, {c3} or {c4} on OpenAI, {c5}) with failover between them. Send the recording as multipart form data: {c6} (required; mp3, mp4/m4a, wav, ogg/opus, webm, flac…, up to 25 MB), {c7} (optional ISO code such as {c8} or {c9}, helps accuracy), {c10} (optional words or names to spell right), and {c11} ({c12}, the default, or {c13} for the bare transcript). The text stays in the language spoken; it is not translated.
docs.transcribeSdk: {c1} is optional and, as everywhere, only {c2} is accepted. With the OpenAI SDK (client set up as below):
docs.modelsHelp: Returns a single {c1} entry, OpenAI-style — the gateway always picks the provider/model itself.
docs.sdkHelp: Point any OpenAI-compatible SDK at this gateway by overriding its base URL — this also makes it a drop-in OpenRouter replacement.
